policy_date: Undated in the policy body; released to ASX as a revised policy on 5 February 2021
covered_persons: Section 3 (insider trading, unvested hedging ban, short-term trading ban) applies to all Westpac Directors, directors of controlled entities, and all employees, secondees and contractors in Australia and overseas. Section 4 (blackouts, notification/approval, margin loans, short selling, blackout exceptions) applies only to Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees (including Group Executives and Key Prescribed Employees). Both extend to 'associates' and 'employee related accounts' (spouse/partner, dependent children, family trusts, controlled companies, entities of which the person is a director/secretary/executive officer).
closed_periods: Two Blackout Periods: (1) from 15 March until the beginning of trading in Sydney one day after announcement of half-year results in early May; (2) from 15 September until the beginning of trading in Sydney one day after announcement of full-year results in early November. The Chief Compliance Officer may extend or reduce these, conditionally or unconditionally.

derivatives.detail: 'Securities' expressly includes derivatives and options, so insider trading and Blackout Period rules apply to them. Options/derivatives that limit economic risk on unvested holdings are prohibited for everyone; over vested holdings they are not prohibited but, for Directors and Prescribed Employees, are subject to the Section 4 approval/notification/pre-clearance regime for 'hedging arrangements over vested Westpac securities'.
derivatives.evidence: You must not enter into any options, derivatives or other arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in Westpac securities ... This prohibition does not apply to vested holdings in Westpac securities, although approval or notification and other arrangements apply to Directors and Prescribed Employees dealing in vested securities

hedging_unvested.detail: All Directors and Employees (Section 3 applies group-wide) are prohibited from any option, derivative or other arrangement that limits the economic risk of unvested Westpac securities or unvested entitlements under employee share plans.
hedging_unvested.evidence: You must not enter into any options, derivatives or other arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in Westpac securities or other unvested entitlements under employee share plans.

hedging_vested.detail: Hedging vested holdings is expressly not prohibited. Outside a Blackout Period, Westpac Directors need the Chairman's prior approval (Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman) and must notify the Company Secretary immediately afterwards; Prescribed Employees must lodge a Trade Notification Form beforehand; Key Prescribed Employees must obtain pre-clearance under the separate Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process. No hedging of vested securities is permitted during a Blackout Period or while holding inside information.
hedging_vested.evidence: Westpac Directors must obtain the approval of the Chairman before they or their associates do any of the following outside a Blackout Period: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps and funded/monetised structures are not mentioned. The closest hooks are the 'hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities' approval/notification trigger and the rule that any transaction causing a change in ownership is a 'trade', which would capture any physical delivery or transfer leg.
monetisation.evidence: Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy.

short_selling.detail: Short selling (selling borrowed financial products) by Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees is prohibited and treated as a breach. The clause is in Section 4 so it applies to that tier, not to all employees.
short_selling.evidence: Short selling by Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees is prohibited and will be considered a breach of this Policy.

margin_lending.detail: Directors and Prescribed Employees may take margin loans over Westpac securities, but margin calls may not be met by selling Westpac securities during a Blackout Period or while holding inside information; a lender sale in a Blackout Period is a breach regardless of instruction. Persons are expected to be able to meet calls without selling and are steered toward facilities without price triggers. Key Prescribed Employees must disclose margin lending arrangements to the Group Control Room.
margin_lending.evidence: Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees are permitted to take out margin loans over their holdings in Westpac securities, however margin calls are not to be met by the sale of Westpac securities at a time when they would not be permitted to trade Westpac securities under this Policy.

encumbrance.detail: There is no general rule on pledging, granting security or keeping holdings unencumbered; the only encumbrance treated is a margin loan (permitted, with the sale restrictions above). A bank taking security over the collared shares is therefore not expressly regulated except to the extent it involves a margin facility or a lender-forced sale.
encumbrance.evidence: If your margin lender sells any of your Westpac securities during a Blackout Period, whether on your instructions to do so or not, it will be considered a breach of this Policy.

short_term_trading.detail: Short-term or speculative trading (entry to exit within a few days to a few weeks) is prohibited group-wide; all employees must trade with a medium to long-term perspective. A loss-avoiding early sale may be possible with Group Control Room guidance.
short_term_trading.evidence: Short-term or speculative trading is prohibited and all employees must conduct their personal trading activities with a medium to long term perspective.

approval.approver: Chairman for Westpac Directors (Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman); pre-clearance under the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process (an Addendum not included in the document) for Key Prescribed Employees; other Prescribed Employees need only give prior notification to the Group Control Room via the online Prescribed Employee Trade Notification Form.
approval.post_trade_notification: Westpac Directors must notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading by themselves or associates, including entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities. Directors or Group Executives granted a Blackout Period exception must advise the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive and the Company Secretary to assist with any Appendix 3Y.
approval.evidence: Westpac Directors must obtain the approval of the Chairman before they or their associates do any of the following outside a Blackout Period: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities ... Westpac Directors must also notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading

exceptional_circumstances.detail: Directors and Prescribed Employees facing an unreasonable financial impost or other exceptional circumstances may apply in writing (Directors to the Chairman; Chairman to the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee; Group Executives, Key Prescribed and Prescribed Employees to the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive) for an exemption from the ban on selling in a Blackout Period. The exception is framed around a sale or disposal only, not hedging, and the decision-maker must decline if they hold inside information.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees who have an unreasonable financial impost or who are in other exceptional circumstances may apply in writing to be exempted from the prohibition on selling Westpac securities during a Blackout Period.

other_collar_relevant_clauses: 'Securities' include ... derivatives; or options; or ... any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market (s3.2) - a collar is therefore a 'security' for blackout and insider trading purposes.

The prohibition on hedging is limited to arrangements which 'operate to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in Westpac securities or other unvested entitlements under employee share plans' (s3.4); it 'does not apply to vested holdings'.

Trigger wording for Directors and Prescribed Employees is 'entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities' or 'arrange for another person to enter into arrangements of those kinds' (ss4.4, 4.6) - so both the executive and an associate/trust entering the collar are caught.

'Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy' (s4.4) - physical settlement, delivery to the bank at expiry, or transfer of shares into a custody/security structure could each be a 'trade' needing separate approval or notification and must not fall in a Blackout Period.

Key Prescribed Employees 'are subject to the requirements as set out in the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process, which is an Addendum to this Policy' (s4.2) - the addendum is not part of the published document, so pre-clearance mechanics for senior executives cannot be verified from this text.

Chief Compliance Officer 'has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered' (s4.3) - an ad hoc restriction could prevent entry, roll or unwind of a collar.

Margin calls 'are not to be met by the sale of Westpac securities' in a Blackout Period; persons 'should take steps to rearrange their affairs to have a facility that does not contain price triggers' (s4.8) - relevant if the collar is funded or the bank takes security with price-triggered enforcement.
Short-term trading ban (s3.5) requires 'a medium to long term perspective' - a short-dated collar or one unwound within weeks could be characterised as speculative.
Directors 'should seek guidance from the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive or the General Manager, Company Secretary' (s6).
collar_assessment: Yes, in principle. Section 3.4 expressly carves vested holdings out of the derivatives/hedging ban, and Sections 4.4-4.6 contemplate 'entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities', so a purchased put / written call over vested shares is a contemplated transaction. A Westpac Director must first obtain the Chairman's approval (or the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee if the Chairman) and then notify the Company Secretary immediately; a Key Prescribed Employee (most senior executives) needs pre-clearance under an unpublished addendum; other Prescribed Employees only need to lodge a prior notification. The collar cannot be entered, rolled or physically settled during either Blackout Period (15 March to post-half-year results; 15 September to post-full-year results) or under an ad hoc restriction, and the collar must not cover any unvested shares or unvested plan entitlements. Monetisation and security/encumbrance are not addressed, so any funded leg should be structured to avoid margin-style price-triggered sales and any share transfer to the bank should be treated as a separate 'trade'.
